title: An apple falls
question: How do height and velocity change as an apple falls from rest?
learningObjectives: Read position/height and velocity as quantities that change with time.
Relate the slope of the height-time graph to velocity.
Relate the slope of the velocity-time graph to constant acceleration.
Recognize that the model's result depends on declared assumptions and coordinate sign.
assumptions: One-dimensional vertical motion with upward-positive coordinates.
Constant acceleration of -9.81 m/s^2 for the entire experiment.
The initial height is selected so the analytical model reaches ground level at one second.
limitations: No air resistance, wind, apple rotation, branch separation, deformation, or ground-contact response.
Tree and apple artwork are explanatory illustration, not physical geometry.
The model is an ideal teaching example, not a claim about every real fall.

visualizations.description: The apple markers and height/velocity plots are tied to the recorded run; tree artwork is illustrative.

validation.method: Run the existing constant-acceleration experiment with declared SI inputs, then check the recorded duration, sample count, final position, and final velocity against analytical expectations.
acceptance: 11 states including the initial state and 10 completed steps.
One second of recorded logical time.
Final position is zero within floating-point tolerance.
Final velocity is -9.81 m/s within floating-point tolerance.
Every displayed state label in the SVG matches a state in the actual run record.
